items.title: Log canonical centers are uniformly perfectoid compatible in the complete normal quasi-Gorenstein setting
items.difficulty_reason: After all existing2373/886 compatibility, conductor, splitting-prime and etale work is given, the author still carries the root-cover derived-pullback and duality argument connecting root purity to log canonicity at both p-containing and p-inverted primes. The finite G1/S2 modification, divisor-rounding trace-image control and localization without p-completeness are essential source-local adaptations beyond routine definition expansion. These support H2. The cited mature perfectoid/duality inputs and adaptations do not justify an additional H3 designation here.

readability.basis: Existing completeofficial36page article; Root viewed cover/rootpurity/deriveddiagrams/duality/bothprimeregimes andTheorem4.12 pages; no newcompile

R as in native notation341–352: complete Noetherian local (R,m,k), residue characteristic p>0, fixed Cohen-ring embeddings and module-finite presentation A=C_k[[x_1,...,x_d]], R_infty^A=(R tensor_A A_infty)_perfd; all choices retained literally.
R is quasi-Gorenstein and normal; p-fraktur is a prime defining a log canonical center in the exact definition798–800.
No additional global perfectoid-purity assumption is inserted in937–939; that assumption belongs to the separate multiplier-ideal corollary958–960.

Both primes containing the residue characteristic p (896–906) and primes not containing p with h in p-fraktur (908–935) are retained. Each root-purity-to-lc proposition also retains the zero-rounddown requirement.

This is author-material scope/difficulty/fidelity acceptance, not an independent correctness certificate. Native942 and officialphysical21 both say generators of maximal ideal m; that literal is retained rather than replaced by the lc-center prime. The named criterion and complete two prime-regime proofs are supplied as authored.
